neighbours.label: the object of a value-laden choice or change in persuasive prose (either strengthen or weaken, create change, see it as an opportunity), as against neutral factual statements
fire: What we eat each day can either protect or damage the heart.
Good leaders do not wait for change; they create it.
Many students see the exchange year as a chance to grow.

We cannot expect progress if we keep making the same choices.
She saw the failure as an opportunity to start again.
Words can either heal or wound the people around us.
quiet: What we eat each day is listed in a small notebook.

Many students spend the exchange year in Spain.
A single conversation took place in the corridor.
Small shops close early on Sundays in this town.
We bought the same bread at the corner bakery.
She moved to a new flat near the river last year.
The words were printed in blue ink on the cover.
